newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE TO FIRMER ON TUESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE TO FIRMER ON TUESDAY.

text.p: HARARE, June 17 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer in fairly quiet trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
The market opened with a Z$22.5 million deficit but liquidity was improved with the maturity of some Z$450 million worth of treasury bills, leaving the market "fairly comfortable" dealers said.
They said the central Reserve Bank auctioned 91-day treasury bills amounting to Z$390 million at an average rate of 24.98 percent, up from 24.86 percent the previous day.
Dealers say despite a fall in annual inflation to 20.7 percent in the year to May from 22.4 percent in April, interest rates are likely to maintain an upward trend in the long term.
On Tuesday, treasury bills were being traded on the secondary market at 24.25 percent while call money was quoted unchanged at 22 percent.
NCD bills with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 25 from 26 percent but sold at a stable 25 percent.
Bank acceptance bills were also quoted steady at 25 percent (buying) and at 24.5 percent on the sell-side.
